answer: A wharf only lets a ship dock after it has crossed the river under its own power, and an agent economy can work the same way: before a new identity can trade, it must solve a proof-of-work puzzle bound to its public key and a recent ledger kernel, a hash the network rotates each epoch. One puzzle is cheap for a real agent, but a sybil army must pay the compute for every fake identity it launches, so faking a thousand voices costs a thousand puzzles of hardware and electricity, and identities that stop working lose their place.
